basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 6.' and it opens 'VERS. 6.-- Post quadraginta dies aperuit Noe fenestram, et emisit corvum, qui'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 6.-- Post quadraginta dies aperuit Noe fenestram, et emisit corvum, qui egrediebatur et non revertebatur. In Hebraeo scriptum est exiens et revertens, donec siccarentur aquae de terra. Sed ideo, ut nostra translatio innuit, non est reversus, quia aut ab aquis est absorptus et interemptus, aut aliquo cadavere supernatante est illectus, et desuper sedere est delectatus, quod columba naturaliter refugit, de qua dicitur: quae cum non invenisset ubi requiesceret | pes ejus, reversa est ad eum in arcam. Verumtamen requirendum est cur quadragenario numero pluvia inundabat, et iterum post quadraginta dies dicitur Noe fenestram arcae aperuisse? Quadragenarius enim iste spiritaliter tribulationem poenitentiae ostendit. Quod vero post quadraginta dies fenestram aperuit, significat jejunio coelum reserari. Ideo Moyses et Elias, etiam et ipse Salvator, jejunia consecravit, tanquam tribus temporibus necessaria ante legem, sub lege, sub gratia. Sequitur:
